subject: Model improvement opt-out & subprocessors — DPA redlines
messages:
From: Sophie Lane <sophie.lane@medsys.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Legal Team <legal@medsys.com>
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA questions — model training, ownership, and subprocessors

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the product looked promising. Before we move to an enterprise contract, our legal/privacy team has a few non-negotiables we need clarified in the DPA/contract:

1) No-training/no-use for model improvement: MedSys cannot have any customer-provided prompts or responses used to further train or tune models that would be accessible outside our tenancy. We need explicit contractual language stating that Redwood will not use our data for model improvement unless we opt in.

2) Prompt/response IP and ownership: confirmation that MedSys retains ownership of inputs and outputs and that Redwood has only the limited license to provide inference.

3) Subprocessors & transfers: current list of subprocessors, notification process for additions, and whether you rely on any processors that transfer data outside the US/EU (we have EU patients).

4) SCCs / transfer mechanism: if data leaves the EU, we need SCCs or equivalent.

I attached an annotated DPA redline (DPA_Redline_v3.docx) with our proposed clauses. Can we get an initial response from your legal team and confirmation whether the no-training commitment is something Redwood will accept for customers on enterprise plans?

Thanks — Sophie
Sophie Lane
Head of Privacy, MedSys Health
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Lane <sophie.lane@medsys.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA questions — model training, ownership, and subprocessors

Hi Sophie — appreciate the clear list and the annotated redline, very helpful. Looping in Mina from Legal and Marissa from Customer Success who will help scope the implementation details.

High level: Redwood supports an explicit model-improvement opt-out for enterprise customers and can amend the DPA to reflect no-training unless you opt in. There are some operational details (hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) we should align on since the promise differs slightly by deployment mode — Mina will follow up with suggested language and details on subprocessors and transfer mechanisms.

We aim to review your redlines and provide counter language by EOD Wednesday. If agreeable, we can also set a short call this week to walk through the changes.

Best,
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Lane <sophie.lane@medsys.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 08:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA questions — model training, ownership, and subprocessors

Sophie — thanks for sending the redline. I reviewed MedSys' proposed language and put together a response summary plus specific contract text (see below).

Summary responses:
- No-training / model improvement: Redwood can commit, for enterprise agreements, that customer-provided prompts, outputs, and other content will not be used to train or improve models that are accessible to other customers or to Redwood's general model catalog unless Customer provides explicit opt-in in writing. This applies to our hosted API offering for customers who select the "No Model Improvement" option on their contract and in the Console. It does not change telemetry needed for service-level monitoring (anonymized metrics).

- Ownership: We will include an explicit statement that you retain ownership of inputs and outputs and that Redwood's rights are limited to providing inference and any operational uses necessary to provide the service (debugging, support) under strict access controls.

- Subprocessors: Attached is the current subprocessors list and SOC 2 attestation we can provide. Redwood requires the ability to engage subprocessors (cloud infra, monitoring, SRE) but will provide 30 days' notice and an objection process for high-risk transfers.

- Cross-border transfers / SCCs: We support execution of SCCs for EU transfers and can provide a DocuSign envelope for signature. For dedicated/private deployments where data remains in-customer cloud/VPC, transfers are controlled by the customer's infra.

Proposed contract snippet (for DPA):
"Customer Data; Use for Model Improvement" — "Redwood will not use Customer Data to develop, train, or improve models that are accessible to other customers or to Redwood's general model catalog unless Customer provides an explicit written opt-in. Operational telemetry (aggregated/anonymized metrics for monitoring and capacity planning) may be collected and will not be used to train models. For clarity, Customer retains all rights, title and interest in Customer Data and Output."

Implementation notes:
- For hosted customers who opt out, we toggle an account-level flag that prevents Customer Data from entering model improvement pipelines. This is currently a contractual plus-product feature (customers on enterprise SKUs).
- For Dedicated clusters, we can commit in the contract to not export prompts/responses from the customer's dedicated environment to any shared training pipelines.
- For Private/on-prem, customer controls the environment and Redwood will not access data for training without explicit opt-in.

Next steps: we can accept the majority of your redlines but have a few suggested edits around definitions and the notification cadence for subprocessors. Would you like the DPA with inline comments or a clean counter-redline?

Regards,
Mina Haddad
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Sophie Lane <sophie.lane@medsys.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@medsys.com>
Date: Fri, 15 May 2026 11:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA questions — model training, ownership, and subprocessors

Mina — thanks for the detailed response and the proposed snippet — that addresses most of our concerns. A few follow-ups from our side after internal review:

1) We need the opt-out to be enforceable contractually without an additional engineering dependency for us to prove compliance. Can Redwood provide periodic attestations (quarterly) that our account has not been used in model training pipelines if we choose no-improvement?

2) Subprocessors: please share the current list in a CSV and confirm if you use any analytics vendors that could ingest raw prompts (we prefer names rather than general categories). Also clarify the objection process: is it 30 days to respond and immediate suspension if we object?

3) SCCs: please send the SCCs DocuSign link so our legal team can execute.

Attached is a brief annotated redline with two small wording tweaks to your proposed snippet (we kept your intent but tightened the audit/attestation expectations).

Can you confirm an approximate timeline for signed DPA + SCCs? We are working toward a June 1 go-live.

Best,
Sophie
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Lane <sophie.lane@medsys.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 14:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA questions — model training, ownership, and subprocessors

Sophie — quick update and confirmation on timelines:

- Mina's team will produce a clean counter-redline with the attestation language included (quarterly statement confirming no-customer-data used for model training when opt-out is selected). Expect that counter by EOD Tuesday.
- Subprocessors CSV and SOC2 report: Marissa will share the current list and a secure link to the SOC2 report within 24 hours. The objection process is: Redwood will notify 30 days prior to onboarding a new subprocessor; if a customer objects within that period, we escalate to legal to attempt mitigation; suspension of the subprocessor is considered only if mutually agreed by both parties or per specific contractual remedy language — we cannot guarantee unilateral immediate suspension of a core cloud infra subprocessor. We'll capture this in the DPA language.
- SCCs: Mina will push the DocuSign envelope today for your team to sign.

We're aligned on the June 1 target for provisioning the environment; signing the DPA + SCCs asap will keep that date intact. If you prefer, we can schedule a 30-minute legal-to-legal call to finalize redlines.

Thanks — Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
